title: Techno-Economic Assessment of Solar Tunnel Fruit Drying in Central Vietnam
content: Solar tunnel drying may reduce postharvest losses and create value-added products for small agricultural enterprises in central Vietnam. This study assessed the techno-economic feasibility of a Hohenheim-type solar tunnel dryer by comparing imported and locally manufactured equipment under two production scenarios: banana only (Mono) and a diversified fruit assortment (Eco). A ten-year discounted cash-flow model included fruit opportunity costs, preparation labour, packaging, distribution, maintenance, component replacements and residual values. The assumed initial investments were 225.9 million VND for the imported dryer and 60.0 million VND for local manufacture. All four combinations yielded positive net present values of 832–1,265 million VND and simple payback periods of 0.41–1.94 years. Mono outperformed Eco financially, while diversification could offer marketing benefits for agritourism not captured in the model. Sensitivity tests for the locally manufactured Eco case retained positive net present values under the individual adverse assumptions examined. The results demonstrate modelled economic potential rather than measured commercial returns. Local trials and market validation are needed to verify drying capacity, product quality and achievable sales.
